I've fixed the floating-point precision bug. The issue was in `src/money.js`: when converting prices like 39.95 to cents by multiplying by 100, JavaScript's floating-point arithmetic produced 3995.0000000000005 instead of exactly 3995. I added `Math.round()` to both price parsing functions to ensure whole cents.

The fix is tested and working—all 50 existing tests pass, and your commands now work:
- ✅ `subtrack add Gym 39.95` works
- ✅ Netflix (12.99) and Spotify (10.99) still work

Ready to commit this change?
